A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DyGMamba. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original link-prediction, synthetic-data, ablation, efficiency, and dynamic node-classification results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds ablation comparisons, MOOC sensitivity results, and discrete-time graph evaluations.

M1.justification: The reported SSM discretization changes from exp(ΔA−I) to exp(ΔA)−I in the node- and time-level blocks (v2 Eqs. 4c/6c; v3 Eqs. 3c/5c). This is a formula-level correction; the architecture, information selection, predictor, and loss remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Appendix L newly evaluates six discrete-time graph datasets: Flights, Can. Parl., US Legis., UN Trade, UN Vote, and Contact. This substantially extends coverage to graphs with concurrent edges, beyond the retained continuous-time and synthetic datasets.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 add Variants C and D as comparison methods that perform information selection without temporal-pattern modeling. The ten external baselines are retained; the discrete-time evaluations reuse that comparator set.

E3.justification: New configurations include the C/D controls, a MOOC patch-size sweep over 4, 2, and 1 with 128 neighbors, and discrete-time dataset settings including a k search up to 200. Existing splits, metrics, training budgets, and selected CTDG hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new C/D ablations test whether benefits arise from generic or opposite-node information selection rather than temporal-pattern modeling, on both real and synthetic data. Appendix J adds MOOC patch-size sensitivity, while Appendix C.1 newly reports qualitative findings from varying γ.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs with five random seeds and report means with error bars. Added results follow existing reporting practices; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 adds C/D results, MOOC sensitivity curves, and extensive discrete-time AP/AUC-ROC results in Tables 18–21. Table 5 changes Variant A's S3 AP from 76.36±0.45 to 77.61±2.31. Figure 2 also revises CTAN's LastFM points to agree with Table 1. Retained Tables 1, 2, and 12–16 have unchanged result rows.

T1.justification: v3 corrects SSM parameter dimensions and discretization, adds a convolution-form expression in Eq. 2, and supplies explicit Transformer/Mamba complexity formulas in Eq. 8. These extend and correct the mathematical treatment without adding new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: SSM-based CTDG learning, temporal-pattern-guided information selection, strong link-prediction performance, and efficient long-history modeling. The discrete-time experiments are explicitly supplementary.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations separating information selection, opposite-node information, and temporal-pattern benefits. It develops the patch-size tradeoff between additional parameters and lost temporal detail. Appendices I, K, and L add motivation for time-level SSMs and explain concurrent-edge limitations and weaker discrete-time performance.

D1.justification: v3 adds operator explanations, the γ search range, and discrete-time hyperparameter information. However, Appendix L lists seven neighbor/patch pairs for six datasets, leaving the full mapping ambiguous. The conclusion also removes v2's code-as-supplementary-material disclosure; actual code availability cannot be determined from these PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds positioning against graph SSM work by Wang et al., Behrouz and Hashemi, and Li et al. (2024b). Zhu et al. (2024) is added for complexity analysis, while Besta et al.'s HOT reference is removed. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 expands SSM and efficiency explanations, introduces numbered subsections within Sections 4.2–4.3, and reorganizes the complexity discussion. It also adds an equal-contribution author note. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document adopts different typography, margins, heading styles, and table placement throughout. Tables 3–5 expand, Figure 2 is redrawn, and Figure 7 and Tables 17–21 are added. Existing figures are also resized or relocated, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2's Variant A simultaneously removed temporal-pattern modeling and dynamic selection, weakening attribution of their benefits. v3's C/D controls substantially strengthen validation of the central mechanism, while discrete-time evaluations and explicit limitations clarify applicability. These gains outweigh localized documentation problems, including the ambiguous hyperparameter mapping, the convolution/element-wise terminology inconsistency in Eq. 2, and removal of the code-supplement disclosure.
